note: Evaluate mode is read-only; design mode may propose but not apply. All scenarios use checked-in fixtures, not live repositories or hosted accounts. Fixture facts are synthetic unless explicitly marked otherwise. Grade observable decisions, not report layout or exact durations.

evals.name: latency-with-a-deploy-gate
evals.prompt: Our PR checks take a while. Use the supplied evidence to explain the bottleneck and worthwhile options. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Finds the dominant verify test step, distinguishes measured evidence from estimates, and preserves named required-check and deployment dependencies.
assertions: no_changes_or_paid_actions: makes no edits, installs, or hosted changes
dominant_step: identifies pnpm verify as the primary latency contributor
ruleset_authority: uses ruleset evidence rather than empty classic protection
preserves_deploy_edges: retains verify identity and migrate ordering because Railway consumes the suite
separates_run_classes: does not pool PR and push evidence
labels_savings: distinguishes measured, bounded, and estimated savings

evals.name: minutes-not-latency
evals.prompt: Our private repo's Actions bill is rising. Use these evidence files to find consumption drivers; cost matters more than latency.
evals.expected_output: Frames the answer around attempts and billed minutes; counts push and strict-update reruns and names consumers before proposing to trim a run.
assertions: consumption_first: prioritizes raw or billed minutes
strict_update_reruns: recognizes reruns after main advances
main_run_consumers: identifies Railway and migrate consumers
raw_vs_billed: distinguishes runner duration from per-job rounded billed time
parallelism_tradeoff: explains latency gains may raise total minutes
no_unsourced_rate: does not invent a price

evals.name: nothing-worth-changing
evals.prompt: Audit the supplied CI evidence. What should we speed up or cut?
evals.expected_output: Concludes that the three fast jobs on a public repo do not warrant churn, preserving validate and network-dependent builder-agrees separation.
assertions: little_to_gain: recommends no meaningful change
public_unbilled: correctly cites public hosted-runner economics in fixture
three_job_facts: uses the three fixture jobs, not the stale two-job claim
keeps_builder_separate: respects network-dependent failure isolation
no_invented_optimization: avoids meaningful cache, matrix, filter, or sharding claims

evals.name: design-without-history
evals.prompt: Design an initial CI architecture for this new repository. There is no run history; give a practical design and a way to validate it.
evals.expected_output: Makes a deliberate design from the repository profile, marks unknowns, avoids fabricated measurements, and supplies staged validation and decision criteria.
assertions: designs_despite_no_history: proposes a coherent initial event/task/gate design
profile_drives_choices: adapts to small team, release and assurance needs
no_fabricated_measurements: labels estimates and unknowns
event_gate_contracts: names event, tested revision, gate and artifact identity
exact_native_commands: proposed invocations use the fixture's actual npm script names, including any generated matrix commands
revision_matches_checkout: stated tested revisions agree with the proposed provider event and checkout, or remain explicitly unresolved until provider choice
validation_plan: proposes collecting a baseline and revisiting decisions
simplicity_tradeoff: avoids unjustified platform or component complexity

evals.name: shared-runner-saturation
evals.prompt: PR feedback is slow. Diagnose this synthetic runner-pool evidence and recommend the smallest useful next step.
evals.expected_output: Separates dispatch/queue contention from execution, recognizes the shared pool is saturated, and does not blindly add shards or workers.
assertions: shared_capacity: identifies cross-project shared pool contention
separates_queue_compute: does not mislabel queue delay as slow tests
rejects_blind_sharding: notes added parallel tasks worsen slot demand
capacity_evidence: recommends verifying eligible capacity/dispatch before fleet expansion
bounded_impact: estimates latency/consumption separately

evals.name: selection-and-aggregate-gate
evals.prompt: Review the affected-task selector and required aggregate gate in this fixture. State what is unsafe and how to make the gate truthful.
evals.expected_output: Fails broad on unknown or missing comparison evidence and only accepts skipped tasks when selection is validated; failed, cancelled, or absent prerequisites cannot turn the aggregate green.
assertions: unknown_fails_broad: unknown paths or missing base select full suite
transitive_shared_inputs: shared lock/config changes include all affected consumers
aggregate_checks_expected_tasks: gate verifies the expected task set
failure_cancel_missing_block: failed, cancelled, and missing prerequisites are non-green
skip_requires_valid_selection: skipped task accepted only with validated selector evidence

evals.name: fork-to-privileged-artifact-trust
evals.prompt: Assess whether the proposed fork validation and release artifact flow is safe. Identify the concrete trust boundary and required controls.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes untrusted fork code and artifacts can reach privileged consumers/cache writers; requires isolation, least privilege, identity/digest verification, and promotion tied to exact revision.
assertions: identifies_untrusted_origin: marks fork code and its outputs untrusted
blocks_privileged_reuse: rejects direct privileged execution or writable trusted-cache path
verifies_artifact_identity: checks producer, source revision and digest at consumption
least_privilege_isolation: proposes scoped credentials and isolated runners
no_provenance_overclaim: does not treat upload or checksum alone as trusted provenance

evals.name: native-result-cache-and-gitlab-semantics
evals.prompt: Review this Bazel cache proposal and GitLab pipeline configuration. Which parts are sound, and what must change?
evals.expected_output: Allows Bazel's dependency-aware result reuse with trusted writers and uncached validation while rejecting a forced pass flag; correctly accounts for GitLab duplicate event pipelines, rules:changes, needs artifact identity, and merged-results revisions.
assertions: native_cache_qualified: allows native dependency-aware result caching with correct inputs and trusted cache
unsafe_pass_flag_rejected: rejects arbitrary pass/skip flags
uncached_validation: keeps a cold or uncached correctness path
gitlab_event_semantics: distinguishes push/MR pipeline creation and rules:changes bases
needs_artifact_identity: ties needed artifacts to intended current pipeline producer
merged_revision: distinguishes source-only from merged-results revision

evals.name: implement-with-local-authority
evals.prompt: You may modify only a disposable copy of the supplied fixture. Fix the aggregate gate so failure, cancellation, or missing prerequisites fail closed, keep selection evidence truthful, and run its checker. Do not use hosted services or edit the source fixture.
evals.expected_output: Copies the fixture, changes the broken gate, runs the executable checker successfully, and reports the local-only scope without claiming hosted validation.
assertions: source_fixture_untouched: edits only a disposable copy, not checked-in fixture
aggregate_is_truthful: aggregate rejects failed, cancelled, and missing required prerequisites
valid_skip_only: accepts skip only when selector says valid and justified
checker_passes: executes the included checker against the changed copy
local_authority_only: does not access hosted settings, install, or claim deployment validation

history: Iteration 1 (1 sample per eval; runs in detached worktrees at origin/main so the baseline could not find the skill; reports blinded A/B and graded blind against ground truth from the workflow files; totals from visualize-spec/evals/aggregate.py): skill preferred 3 of 3; assertions 21/21 vs 19/21; accuracy 5.00 vs 4.00, actionability 5.00 vs 4.33, contract_safety 5.00 vs 4.67. Baseline misses: labels_estimates on latency (savings stated without labels) and counts_strict_update_reruns on minutes (said re-runs were negligible). Both configurations kept every deploy-gate contract, so those assertions do not discriminate and should be sharpened or replaced next iteration. Notable differences: on latency the skill declined to start a Postgres container to measure cleanup cost and said so, while the baseline started and removed one unasked; on minutes the skill found draft-PR runs (34 of 136, 585 minutes) and proved 66 of 69 main pushes re-tested a tree that had already passed, which the baseline asserted without counting. Both read the org billing API, so no_rates_from_memory passed both ways. Residual blinding tell: with-skill command logs reference a collector script the baselines never used. Harness note: subagents cannot write report files here, so runs returned reports as messages and the orchestrator saved them.
